problem_1_medgemma_12b.likely_source_of_the_12b_belief: Gemma 3 (the base family MedGemma is built on) does ship a 12B: gemma3:12b. MedGemma's medical post-training was only ever applied to the 4B and 27B Gemma 3 checkpoints. A 12B MedGemma would have to be trained, not downloaded.
problem_1_medgemma_12b.why_it_goes_back_to_her: Her instruction ruled out 27B and named 12B as the intended size. 12B does not exist, so the surviving MedGemma options are 4B and 27B - and 27B is the one she excluded. Substituting either one silently would change the model-size arm of the design without her agreeing to it.
what_she_needs_to_decide: MedGemma 4B (medgemma:4b-it-q4_K_M, or medgemma1.5:4b-it-q4_K_M for the newer 1.5 generation), which runs on this hardware; or
MedGemma 27B (medgemma:27b-it-q4_K_M), which does NOT run on this hardware and needs a machine with more memory; or
drop MedGemma and use the 12B she may actually have meant, gemma3:12b, which is the general-purpose Gemma 3 at that size with no medical post-training.

[OPINION] if a 12B substitute is chosen, take gemma3:12b-it-q4_K_M, not gemma4:12b, unless someone first demonstrates gemma4 can be held non-thinking.

problem_2_deepseek_8b.finding: Every 8B DeepSeek that exists is a reasoning model. There is no non-reasoning DeepSeek at 8B.

evidence.result: 8B tags are deepseek-r1:8b, 8b-0528-qwen3-{q4_K_M,q8_0,fp16}, 8b-llama-distill-{q4_K_M,q8_0,fp16}. Both 8B lineages are R1 distills, i.e. reasoning models.

evidence.check: Ollama library capability badge on the deepseek-r1 page
evidence.result: the deepseek-r1 tags page carries the capability badges 'tools' and 'thinking'. The medgemma and medgemma1.5 tags pages carry only 'vision'.
evidence.caveat: the ollama capability flag is template-derived and over-reports. /api/show on qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M returns capabilities ['tools','thinking','completion'] even though that model is the one this project switched TO because it cannot think, and it emits a mean of 60.6 output tokens per call with no think tags across the 830 calls logged so far in runs/debate_20260818.jsonl. So the badge is suggestive, not decisive - the absence of a thinking badge on medgemma is the more informative half, and the 3-case trial below is the arbiter.

evidence.check: Ollama library, every other DeepSeek family
evidence.result: deepseek-r1, deepseek-llm, deepseek-coder, deepseek-coder-v2, deepseek-v2, deepseek-v2.5, deepseek-v3, deepseek-v3.1, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-ocr, deepscaler, r1-1776, openthinker. None of them publishes an 8B non-reasoning chat tag: deepseek-llm is 7b/67b only; deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-pro are cloud-only tags (:cloud, :preview-cloud, :0731-cloud, :0813-cloud) with no local weights; the v2/v2.5/v3/v3.1 families start at 16B and run to 671B.

evidence.check: HuggingFace API, publisher deepseek-ai, full listing
evidence.result: 103 repositories. The only 8B chat models are DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, both reasoning. Non-reasoning DeepSeek chat models nearest in size are deepseek-llm-7b-chat (7B, 2023), deepseek-coder-7b-instruct-v1.5 (code), deepseek-moe-16b-chat and DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (16B MoE). The 8B entries dspark_qwen3_8b_block7 / dflash_qwen3_8b_block7 are speculative-decoding side modules for V4, not standalone chat models.

problem_2_deepseek_8b.thinking_mode_flag: deepseek-r1:8b WILL reintroduce the exact failure class this project spent the night of 18 Aug eliminating. qwen3:4b (hybrid) could not be made non-thinking: think:false relocated reasoning into content, /no_think only moved it to a separate field, and both still spent 1000-1588 output tokens per call. R1 is worse than a hybrid: the R1 distills are trained to always open a reasoning block, and the ollama page declares 'thinking' as a model capability rather than an optional mode.
problem_2_deepseek_8b.decision_owner: user (this is explicitly not decided here)
options_to_put_to_the_supervisor: deepseek-r1:8b, accepting thinking tokens and the token-budget / latency cost, and accepting that the round-0 purity argument now has to cope with a visible reasoning trace.
deepseek-llm:7b-chat-q4_K_M - genuinely non-reasoning, but 7B not 8B, released Nov 2023, and trained at 4096 context.
drop DeepSeek and use a current non-reasoning 8B from another publisher, which is what qwen3:4b-instruct-2507 already is at 4B.

hardware_feasibility.statement: medgemma:27b-it-q4_K_M cannot run on this machine. Its model layer alone is 17.40 GB = 16.20 GiB (17397211520 bytes, from the ollama registry manifest) against an 11.8 GiB Metal budget, before any KV cache and before the qwen3 stage-D model that is already resident. It was therefore not pulled and not trialled - the download would have been 17.4 GB spent to prove a number that the manifest already gives.

does_not_fit: Q3_K_S 12.17 GB = 11.33 GiB (no headroom for KV)
sub_q4_options_if_27b_is_insisted_on.assessment: [OPINION] running a 27B clinical model at Q2 to make it fit is a worse methodological compromise than running 4B at Q4. It also means leaving the ollama registry - the ollama library ships only the multimodal 27b-it, not the text-only medgemma-27b-text-it that this text-only task actually wants - so a 27B route adds an out-of-registry GGUF import and a new provenance problem on top of the quantisation one.

hardware_feasibility.corollary: If Tingting chooses 27B at a defensible quantisation, it needs a different machine. That is a memory-capacity fact, not a scheduling one.
hardware_feasibility.headroom_for_the_pilots_predicted_vs_act: PREDICTED before the trials: qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M resident at 3.9 GB per 'ollama ps', plus medgemma (3.11 GiB) or deepseek-r1 (4.87 GiB), all inside the 11.3 GiB Metal 'available' figure, so no eviction expected. ACTUAL: eviction on every call. The prediction was wrong because ollama gates on system free RAM as well as GPU memory and logged system_limited=true with only 1.7-3.6 GiB of system RAM free. See measurement_caveats.eviction_thrash.

points_that_matter_for_this_project: Section 1.1(a) defines 'Clinical Use' as any use in diagnosis or treatment of patients, including as part of a research study.
Section 3.1 requires that any redistribution carry the Section 3.2 use restrictions as an enforceable provision, ship a copy of the agreement, mark modified files, and include a HAI-DEF notice file.
Section 3.2 prohibits uses listed in the HAI-DEF Prohibited Use Policy and any use that could cause a Health Regulatory Authority to deem Google a medical-device manufacturer.
licensing_note.assessment: [OPINION] retrospective scoring of model recommendations against MIMIC-IV S/I/R, with no patient contact and no clinical deployment, is not diagnosis or treatment of a patient. But this is a licence the report should name explicitly, and it is a stricter licence than the MIT that DeepSeek-R1 ships under.

what_the_tok_per_s_numbers_are_and_are_n.are: generation-only rates: tok/s = eval_count / (eval_duration/1e9), and ollama reports load_duration separately, so the cold-load penalty is NOT inside these figures.
what_the_tok_per_s_numbers_are_and_are_n.are_not: clean benchmarks. They were taken on a memory-pressured, thrashing box. The incumbent's 24.6 tok/s in throughput_measured.csv was taken at 03:36:17 on 18 Aug, before stage D2 started, i.e. uncontended. Comparing 10.17 against 24.6 is therefore biased against the pilot, and the three pilots are only fairly comparable to EACH OTHER, all having been measured under the same conditions.
what_the_tok_per_s_numbers_are_and_are_n.n: 3 calls per model. Every figure below carries n=3.

medgemma:4b-it-q4_K_M.confidence: high on the thinking question, low on the speed question
why: Does not think. /api/show returns capabilities ['completion','vision'] with no 'thinking'. Across 3/3 calls: zero '<think>' occurrences in content, zero characters in the response 'thinking' field, done_reason 'stop' every time. It accepted think:false without error.
Output length is in the same band as the incumbent: eval_count 60, 84, 56 (mean 66.7, n=3) against the incumbent's mean 60.6 over 830 calls in runs/debate_20260818.jsonl. No token-budget blow-up.
Harness-parser compatible: DR.parse_drug returned a valid closed-formulary agent on 3/3 calls (cefazolin each time).
It is the only MedGemma that fits this machine at a defensible quantisation.
against: 10.17 tok/s (n=3) against the incumbent's 24.6 tok/s in throughput_measured.csv - but the pilot number was taken during eviction thrash and the incumbent number was not, so this comparison is not yet fair. Re-measure after stage D.

If 10.17 tok/s survives a clean re-measure, generation alone costs about 6.6 s per call against about 2.5 s for the incumbent; at 10 calls per case (5 turns x 2 orderings) that is roughly 66 s/case of pure generation versus 25 s/case.
4.3B parameters, not 4.0B, because the Gemma 3 vision tower ships inside the same GGUF and this is a text-only task.
Choosing 4B at all is Tingting's decision to make, not a default to fall into - see problem_1_medgemma_12b.

deepseek-r1:8b.confidence: high - the failure is total, not marginal
why_not: think:false did not suppress reasoning. It relocated it. 3/3 calls returned 2233, 2219 and 2292 characters in the response 'thinking' field and ZERO characters in 'content'.
3/3 calls hit the num_predict ceiling: eval_count 512, done_reason 'length'. The model never reached an answer inside the harness's own token budget.
DR.parse_drug returned INVALID on 3/3. In the real harness that fires the retry path, which would fail identically, and the case position would land on INVALID.

4.70 tok/s (n=3) and a mean wall of 138.96 s for ONE call. The harness needs 10 calls per case before retries; that is roughly 23 minutes per case at best and about double that once every call retries. 192 cases is not reachable.
This is the same failure the project already paid for once: model_registry.json records that /no_think on qwen3:4b merely moved reasoning to a separate field. deepseek-r1:8b reproduces it exactly.
deepseek-r1:8b.the_grep_result_is_a_trap: the task asked for a '<think>' grep with zero required. deepseek-r1:8b SCORES ZERO on that grep and still fails completely, because ollama 0.32.14 strips the reasoning into a structured 'thinking' field instead of leaving literal tags in content. The literal-tag count is not a sufficient acceptance test; thinking-field length and done_reason are.
deepseek-r1:8b.decision: NOT MINE. Reported, not decided. The user and Tingting choose whether to accept a reasoning model.

deepseek-llm:7b-chat-q4_K_M.viable: on the thinking criterion yes; as a substitute for 'DeepSeek-8B' that is a judgement call, not a technical one
why: Cleanest non-thinking signal of the three: /api/show returns capabilities ['completion'] and nothing else.
3/3 calls: zero '<think>', zero thinking-field characters, done_reason 'stop', eval_count 64/52/57 (mean 57.7, n=3), all parsed to a valid formulary agent (meropenem).

Its 4096 trained context is NOT a blocker: the largest prompt anywhere in the live run is 579 tokens (max prompt_eval_count over 830 calls in runs/debate_20260818.jsonl), so a full 5-turn debate fits with a wide margin.
against: 5.76 tok/s (n=3), slower than the 4B MedGemma despite similar output length.
It is 7B, not 8B, and it is the DeepSeek LLM of November 2023. Calling it 'DeepSeek-8B' in a report would be wrong.

I ran it at num_ctx 8192 to match the frozen harness options, which is above its trained 4096. That extrapolates RoPE for no benefit; if this model is used, num_ctx should be set to 4096 and the deviation recorded.

All 3 cases got meropenem where MedGemma gave cefazolin on the same 3 cases. At n=3 and temperature 0 that is not evidence of anything, but a carbapenem-by-default prior versus a narrow-spectrum prior is exactly the axis the S/I/R arbiter scores, so it needs a real n before anyone reads meaning into it.

medgemma:27b-it-q4_K_M.why_not: 17.40 GB model layer against an 11.8 GiB Metal budget on this machine. Not pulled - the download would have cost 17.4 GB to confirm a number the registry manifest already states. See hardware_feasibility.

recommended_next_steps: Put the MedGemma size question back to Tingting with the fact that 12B does not exist. Do not substitute silently.
Put the deepseek-r1:8b numbers to the user and let them decide; do not adopt a reasoning model by default.
Re-run this exact 3-case trial after stage D finishes, on an idle machine, so the tok/s figures are clean. The script takes one argument list: _cc_pilot_trial.py <tag> [<tag> ...].

If MedGemma 4B is chosen, decide between medgemma:4b-it-q4_K_M and the newer medgemma1.5:4b-it-q4_K_M before freezing a second registry entry. medgemma1.5:4b-it-q4_K_M was NOT pulled in this session (the pull was paused at 9% to free bandwidth for the three requested models).
No further model pilots on this machine while stage D is running.
